annotationRationale: Factorial divisibility depends on having the required prime factors. The factor 23 forces the lower bound, while factors 8, 11, and 23 establish sufficiency.
sourceMethod: Follows the official prime-factorization method, explaining both why smaller factorials fail and why 23! contains enough of every required prime.

review.mathCheck: Since 2024=2^3·11·23, n<23 supplies no prime factor 23. Conversely, 23! contains the distinct factors 8,11,23, whose product is 2024. The least value is 23, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Original wording faithfully expands official Q5 on page 3: factor 2024, establish the threshold imposed by 23, and verify sufficiency.
review.annotationCheck: The factorial-divisibility assessment is an elementary first-power instance. It does not establish mastery of general prime-power counts or trailing-zero problems.
